reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the formation of a dense oxide and improved corrosion resistance at ~10 at.% Al, but the hypothesis extrapolates this to high-temperature steam oxidation (~800°C) without direct evidence, and the cited study tested under PWR operational conditions, not accident conditions.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coatings with ~10 at.% Al form a dense oxide layer of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2
This oxide layer provides the best corrosion resistance and minimum oxygen penetration depth
The coating can be applied to zirconium-alloy cladding by RF magnetron co-sputtering
The performance was evaluated under PWR operation conditions, not high-temperature steam accident conditions
